chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah from Hasan ibn Ali al-Zaituni from al-Zuhri al-Kufi from Banan ibn Hamdawayh said:

The passing away of my father Ja'far (peace be upon him) was mentioned before Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him). He said: 'That is so long as I am alive and remaining. However, how would it be like when they miss the one after me?'

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: my father Ja'far (referring to Imam al-Naqi)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Askari say about the community's condition after his death?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Askari (AS) contrasts the temporary nature of his own life with the enduring spiritual void the community will face after his death, foreshadowing the Great Occultation. This narration highlights the transition from the visible leadership of the Imams to the period of concealment, emphasizing the believers' reliance on the Imam's presence even when unseen. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the psychological and theological preparation of the Shia community for the era of Ghayba.
